item.title: Kinosaki Onsen: The Willow-Lined Hot Spring Town — Guide
item.description: Kinosaki Onsen, on the Sea of Japan coast of northern Hyogo, is the most complete and atmospheric hot spring town in the country. A willow-lined canal runs through its centre, crossed by little stone bridges and flanked by wooden inns, and the whole town is built around a single idea: guests stay in a ryokan but bathe out in the town, wandering between seven public bathhouses in yukata and clattering wooden geta.

item.title: Bessho Onsen: A Historic Hot Spring Town Called 'Little Kamakura' — Guide
item.description: Bessho Onsen is one of Japan’s oldest hot spring towns, its waters used since ancient times, and today combines traditional public bathhouses and ryokan with an unusual concentration of important historic temples, pagodas and Buddhist statues dating from the Kamakura period, earning it the nickname the ‘Kamakura of Shinshu’. This blend of restorative hot springs and cultural heritage, set in a quiet valley in eastern Nagano, makes it a rewarding destination for travellers wanting to combine a relaxing soak with genuine historical sightseeing.

item.title: Gero Onsen: One of Japan's Three Great Hot Springs — Guide
item.description: Gero Onsen has been ranked among Japan’s three greatest hot springs since the Edo period, prized for its smooth, skin-softening alkaline waters, and sits in a scenic river valley conveniently located on the rail line between Nagoya and Takayama. The town is built around the Hida River, lined with ryokan and public bathhouses, and offers several free foot baths scattered along the streets and riverbank, plus a riverside open-air bath, making it easy to sample the famous waters whether staying overnight or passing through.

item.title: Awara Onsen: Fukui's Premier Hot Spring Resort Town — Guide
item.description: Awara Onsen is Fukui’s most prominent hot spring resort town, having welcomed guests for over 130 years since its waters were first developed in the late 19th century, and today offers numerous ryokan, public bathhouses and a relaxed resort atmosphere. Its convenient location near the coast makes it a natural base for winter Echizen crab trips and sightseeing at nearby Tojinbo Cliffs, and a foot bath in the town centre offers a free, casual way to sample the waters even for day visitors not staying overnight.

item.title: Yamanaka Onsen: A Gorge-Side Hot Spring Town Praised by Basho — Guide
item.description: Yamanaka Onsen was praised by the famed 17th-century haiku poet Matsuo Basho for its restorative waters during his travels through the region, and the town retains a genuine literary and historical atmosphere alongside its traditional hot spring bathhouses. Beyond the baths, visitors can walk the scenic Kakusenkei Gorge trail along the Daishoji River, cross the striking red Korogi Bridge, and browse shops connected to Kutani porcelain, one of the Kaga region’s celebrated ceramic craft traditions.

item.title: Yamashiro Onsen: A 1,300-Year-Old Hot Spring Town — Guide
item.description: Yamashiro Onsen is one of the Kaga region’s oldest hot spring towns, its waters discovered some 1,300 years ago according to local tradition, and the town today centres on Kosoyu, a beautifully restored public bathhouse rebuilt in the style of the Meiji-era original, alongside the still-functioning Soyu bathhouse next door. The town also has strong ties to Kutani porcelain, one of Japan’s most celebrated ceramic traditions, with a small museum and shops nearby offering a look at the distinctive, richly coloured pottery style associated with the region.
